requirements.requirement: Publish the staged public and staff trees at /public/ and /staff/ on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Apache is configured for the two staged directories, listens on *:8080, and remained active with the listener present after restart. Direct HTTP probes returned the staged content.

requirements.requirement: Allow anonymous access to public pages and keep the supplied pages intact.
requirements.summary: Anonymous /public/ requests returned HTTP 200, and the response exactly matched the supplied public index before and after restart. The staff index and roster also exactly matched their supplied files when fetched with valid credentials.

requirements.requirement: Require HTTP Basic authentication as reader with the demonstration password for all staff content, keeping content inaccessible after missing or failed authentication.
requirements.summary: A protected reader credential was generated from access.txt. Valid credentials returned HTTP 200 and exact staff content; anonymous and deliberately incorrect credentials returned HTTP 401 without matching the protected content. Both staff files were exercised.

requirements.requirement: Do not serve password files or directory listings.
requirements.summary: access.txt requests returned 404, including an authenticated staff-path probe. The generated htpasswd file resides outside the aliased trees, and URL probes did not return it. Empty-directory probes returned 403 for public and authenticated staff access.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supplied pages under /srv/legacy2/web-authentication-boundary intact.
requirements.summary: The final source inventory retained access.txt and all three supplied page/data files. HTTP response comparisons showed byte-for-byte matches for public/index.html, staff/index.html, and staff/roster.csv; access.txt retained its root-only permissions.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 before and after implementation and restart. Apache 2.4 packages were installed from the platform's RHEL repositories, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The staged trees are served on port 8080 with the required anonymous/public and authenticated/staff boundary, failed authentication blocks the complete staff tree, credential files and listings are not exposed, supplied content remains intact, and the OS/kernel were preserved. The independent node-restart protocol also directly demonstrated recovery after a changed boot identity.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 against its managed-node IP; no separate external-client reachability probe was captured, although the listener and permanent firewall opening were directly verified.
The final evidence compared every supplied page/data response byte-for-byte but did not repeat a complete filesystem hash and metadata manifest for the whole source tree.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, Apache/authentication configuration, SELinux labeling and port mapping, firewall access, and service enablement were causally necessary to publish and protect the trees. Temporary listing probes and the pre-restart boot-ID marker supported bounded verification and were removed. The required restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart service, acknowledged scheduled restart, observed unavailability, changed boot identity, and recovered service/content/security behavior. No failed services, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue was observed afterward.
